findings.claim: --help/-h, --version/-V, --self-test and --status are matched anywhere in argv, including the wrapped command after `--`. `with-device dev -- probe-rs --version` prints with-device's version and exits 0 without claiming or running the command.

The 'after holder CRASHED' check kills the wrapped `sh` ($$ is sh's pid), not with-device. The holder exits normally and releases the lock, so kernel release on holder crash is never exercised and the check passes even if a crashed holder leaves the device locked.

findings.quoted_line: //! So the self-test discriminates on (a), NOT on (b). Do not read a green self-test as
findings.claim: False claim: with the sort (b) intact and drop-and-retry (a) removed, both processes take selftest-a first, so no cycle forms and the opposite-order test still passes. It fails only when both are removed. It discriminates on neither mechanism alone, and the table omits that variant.

--status probes by actually taking LOCK_EX on every free device and overwriting its .holder file. A real claimant racing it without --wait gets exit 3 'DEVICE BUSY' with holder 'status probe', and nothing is run. A read-only status query can cause refused claims.

try_claim collapses lock-file open errors (EACCES, ENOENT after the ignored create_dir_all failure, EMFILE) and flock errors other than EWOULDBLOCK into Err(()). claim_all reports them as 'DEVICE BUSY ... claimed', exits 3, and with --wait spins until the deadline, so a setup error is hidden.

The holder file is opened with File::create (O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, follows symlinks) in a predictable dir under world-writable /var/tmp. Another local user who pre-creates /var/tmp/pulseengine-bench can symlink <dev>.holder so that a claim truncates and overwrites any file the claimant can write.

The holder JSON is built by hand, and only '"' is replaced. A backslash or newline in BENCH_WHO or --purpose produces invalid JSON, and status --format json embeds the holder verbatim (and the device name unescaped), so its machine-readable output becomes unparseable.
A malformed or missing --wait value (e.g. `--wait 5s`) is silently treated as 0, so the run is fail-fast. USAGE says bad arguments exit 2. The user asked to wait and gets an immediate exit 3 instead.

On workflow_dispatch, build checks out the dispatch ref (the default branch), not inputs.tag, but publish attaches the binaries to that tag with --clobber. Assets built from different source replace the tag's assets. checkout needs `ref: ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref }}`.

The header says varve#130 needs a SIGNED release asset, but the workflow uploads unsigned tarballs and a SHA256SUMS.txt from the same job: no cosign signature, attestation or provenance. The stated consumer requirement is not met.
